svg.text: ▸ D+ tied to D− = BC1.2 dedicated charging port. Phones then draw
more than the 100 mA a data port allows. Works for Android and
current iPhones; very old Apple kit wants a resistor divider instead.
▸ There is NO data connection. This is a power outlet only.
▸ A USB-C SOURCE needs pull-UPS on CC1 and CC2, not the
5.1 k pull-downs a sink uses. 22 k advertises 1.5 A;
▸ Omit them and most devices draw nothing at all.
▸ The USB return carries up to 1 A.
If it shares a track with the pot's
ground, the offset shifts your ADC
reading. Run it back on its own.
1.11 A of a realistic ≈2 A ceiling. The module sits in the fan
airflow, which is exactly where you want it. Expect it warm,
not hot. If it exceeds 60 °C, add a small heatsink.
Firmware v1.2 ramps the fans up over ~0.85 s. For the first
~70 ms after switch-on they run full until the chip boots.
▸ The USB port is dead when SW1 is off. That is deliberate.
or a plain fuse at F2
F1 was 1.5 A in Rev A. The USB port pushes steady draw to 1.16 A, so it must go up.
A PTC at F2 self-resets when a shorted phone cable is unplugged — far better than a glass fuse.
1. Do NOT use the TP4056 here. It is a single-cell lithium charger;
its USB-C connector is an INPUT and sources nothing.
2. C11 220 µF sits AT the socket. Larger values load U1's soft-start
and can stop the buck from starting at all.
3. Trim U1 to 5.10 V — F2 drops ≈0.15 V at 1 A, so the socket still
sees over 4.9 V at full load.
4. D1 is now a REVERSE SHUNT (1N5402G). Normally reverse-biased, so
it carries nothing and costs no voltage. F1 clears on a reversal.
5. RV1 is ratiometric against AVCC; rail sag does not shift fan speed.
6. 22 AWG minimum on +5 V and GND runs. No firmware change.
CHANGE RECORD — REV A → REV B
slow-blow; steady draw is now 1.16 A
1N5402G across the rail: no drop, no heat
offsets the PTC drop at the socket
1.1 A hold PTC in the +5 V feed to J5
220 µF 10 V at the USB socket
USB-A socket, D+ strapped to D−
TP4056 board — wrong device for this job
port is passive; no pins used
